scope: Quake II multiplayer design hypotheses. Transfer to Q1/Q3, SP or different physics requires separate evidence.
status: Evolving rubric; none of these hypotheses has a new human-playtest validation claim.
promotion_policy: A measured descriptor becomes a recommendation only with a documented mechanism, counterexamples, paired procedural experiment, and reviewer evidence. Compile/navigation failures remain hard gates. Distribution tails are questions, never automatic defects.

rules.principle: Connect meaningful destinations with alternative routes and understandable return paths.
rules.mechanism: Players can rotate, retreat and intercept instead of repeatedly retracing a single corridor.
rules.generator_action: Give major combat spaces distinct approaches; connect upper and lower routes to useful destinations; test directed reachability.
rules.counterexample: A short exposed dead end can work when its reward and escape commitment are deliberate.
rules.experiment: Compare the same procedural blockout with one return connection present/absent; retain resource positions and count forced backtracks and meaningful route choices.

rules.principle: Make destinations, exits and route identities readable at movement speed.
rules.mechanism: Distinct silhouettes, materials, height cues and sound reduce navigation effort while preserving tactical uncertainty.
rules.generator_action: Assign spatial identities before texture details; expose landmark cues at decision points and test each spawn-to-landmark journey.
rules.counterexample: Showing every route and opponent from one hub can make the map readable but strategically shallow.
rules.experiment: Hold geometry fixed while changing only landmark/light cues; compare first-time navigation without giving players a route map.

rules.principle: Give each spawn a plausible route to useful equipment and a chance to choose an escape.
rules.mechanism: Recovery opportunities keep map control contestable without making all spawns identical.
rules.generator_action: Audit every spawn, equipment route and attacker approach; record cover, facing and multiple-exit access with the actual player hull.
rules.counterexample: A nearby weapon through a wall can take longer to reach than a distant weapon on an open route; zero spawn-to-spawn LOS does not prove safety.
rules.experiment: Move one spawn behind existing cover without changing item economy; compare recovery and immediate deaths from matched starts.

rules.principle: Put combat, routes and resources on useful height levels, with ways to contest the upper position.
rules.mechanism: Height changes engagement angles, access cost and route commitment when players have reasons to use it.
rules.generator_action: Place objectives/items and entrances at different elevations; construct reachable up/down circuits before adding decorative platforms.
measure: time spent per useful height level
rules.counterexample: A high ceiling, stacked trim or a platform nobody visits adds geometric height without vertical gameplay.
rules.experiment: Move a major resource and its approach onto a validated upper route; compare use of height against the same geometry with all resources on the floor.

rules.principle: Pair strong positions and rewards with readable costs, threats or commitment.
rules.mechanism: Map control matters while the disadvantaged player still has a way to change the state.
rules.generator_action: For each strong position identify a flank, exposed transition, resource cost or timed commitment and test it from both sides.
rules.counterexample: Adding arbitrary exposure to every reward can erase valuable safe recovery spaces.
rules.experiment: Open one alternate approach to a dominant position; compare control duration and reversal opportunities while keeping the main approach unchanged.

rules.principle: Distribute complementary resources to encourage decisions about timing, movement and risk.
rules.mechanism: Useful circuits create contests in several parts of the map instead of allowing one safe position to collect everything.
rules.generator_action: Separate major resources by meaningful route cost, test strong-weapon/armor combinations, and document the exact game module and respawn settings.
rules.counterexample: Maximum spacing can create tedious empty travel and is not a quality objective.
rules.experiment: Compare a clustered major-item pair against a distributed pair on the same map; retain item counts, timers and player starts.

rules.principle: Offer useful close, medium and long engagements with transitions and counter-routes.
rules.mechanism: Different spaces reward different weapons and positioning skills.
rules.generator_action: Design a distribution of combat ranges, break selected long views with geometry, and avoid a uniformly narrow or uniformly open map.
rules.counterexample: A distinctive rail-focused arena may deliberately concentrate long sightlines; the target mode and intended experience matter.
rules.experiment: Change one sightline interruption while preserving routes; compare engagement ranges and weapon choices rather than optimizing ray lengths alone.

rules.principle: Vary space proportions and transitions for a reason, balancing combat, recovery and movement.
rules.mechanism: Alternating compression and openness creates anticipation, pacing and differentiated decisions.
rules.generator_action: Vary playable width, ceiling height and approach angles around explicit spatial roles; use the hull to validate clearances.
rules.counterexample: Random room-size variance can produce awkward leftover space without improving flow.
rules.experiment: Compare role-driven room proportions against uniform rooms with the same route graph and resource budget.

rules.principle: Use a coherent material and architectural language while giving spaces recognizable identities.
rules.mechanism: Consistent construction and differentiated landmarks support both atmosphere and orientation.
rules.generator_action: Specify a small set of material roles, structural motifs, trim rules and landmark exceptions, then review actual engine renders.
rules.counterexample: Texture count cannot measure theme quality; many textures may implement one coherent kit, while one texture may conceal navigation cues.
rules.experiment: Keep geometry fixed and compare two deliberate art-direction passes; ask reviewers to recognize spaces and assess coherence without showing texture counts.

rules.principle: Use lighting to reveal movement and combat cues while preserving the intended atmosphere.
rules.mechanism: Players can see opponents, exits and hazards without losing spatial mood or hierarchy.
rules.generator_action: Validate the compiled light pass and inspect dark corners, bright backgrounds, silhouettes and landmark emphasis through engine screenshots.
rules.counterexample: Uniform brightness can remove atmosphere; nonempty light data and bright lamps do not prove readability.
rules.experiment: Hold camera, display settings and geometry fixed while changing the light hierarchy; compare recognition tasks using engine-written screenshots.

rules.principle: Fit route capacity, equipment and encounter frequency to the intended player count and mode.
rules.mechanism: The map supports useful contact without persistent congestion or long empty periods.
rules.generator_action: Condition size and resource budgets on mode/capacity; test the lower, nominal and upper intended loads separately.
rules.counterexample: An archive recommendation is not a measured capacity limit; a duel layout may behave differently at eight players.
rules.experiment: Run the same map at three loads with identical rules and report the tradeoffs instead of averaging them into one score.

rules.principle: Give each team viable attack, defense and return routes with comparable opportunities.
rules.mechanism: Objective play offers decisions for both teams, including the team recovering from a lost fight.
rules.generator_action: Use the actual CTF module; verify team starts, both flags, base exits, equipment access and carrier routes in both directions.
rules.counterexample: Visual symmetry does not establish equal travel, weapon access or defensive strength.
rules.experiment: Swap teams/sides and test one route change at a time; retain the objective and resource budget.

rules.principle: Make intended movement reliable under the target game's real physics and collision hull.
rules.mechanism: Players can execute intended routes without snagging, unexplained blocks or misleading visual promises.
rules.generator_action: Validate stairs, ramps, jumps, drops, movers and teleporters with explicit ordinary/special-movement requirements and directional reachability.
rules.counterexample: A point ray, visual gap or unbound AAS file cannot establish player traversal.
rules.experiment: Use project-authored narrow-gap, excessive-step, blocked-return and mover-state controls to demonstrate that the relevant validators reject broken routes.

rules.principle: Spend geometry, visibility and effect budgets on gameplay and visual identity that players notice.
rules.mechanism: Stable frame time preserves movement and aiming quality at the intended load.
rules.generator_action: Measure compiled visibility and representative in-engine frame times; budget detail around the worst views and busiest encounters.
rules.counterexample: BSP size, face count or PVS size alone cannot establish performance on a target renderer.
rules.experiment: Compare a costly detail/effect pass enabled and disabled from identical recorded views and player loads.

rules.principle: Generate distinct tactical experiences across seeds while keeping each map coherent.
rules.mechanism: Different topology, height use, item circuits, space rhythms and visual identities sustain replay value.
rules.generator_action: Evaluate a prompt/seed portfolio by gameplay descriptors and blind recognition; detect repeated layouts separately from repeated textures.
rules.counterexample: Random noise, novelty by broken navigation, and copying a reference layout are not useful variety.
rules.experiment: Freeze the prompt/seed matrix; compare before/after map portfolios in blinded pairs, including quality regressions and mode-specific exceptions.

evidence.observation: Compact room partitioning and rotated crosswalk/horseshoe motifs enter the actual default six-candidate pipeline. Nine fixed requests and separate low/high verticality controls retain all outputs, graph signatures, findings and compiler evidence. No model weights or reference profile are retrained.

rules.principle: A shortcut should offer a useful tradeoff while the required ordinary journey remains viable.
rules.mechanism: Lifts exchange distance for waiting and exposed ascent; a physical alternative lets players respond to platform state and enemy control.
rules.generator_action: Audit ordinary routes with lift, teleporter and optional jump edges removed; retain native platform stations, full sweep, boarding/exit space and activation rules.
rules.counterexample: A shortcut so much faster than its bypass can become effectively compulsory; an unused detour is not meaningful counterplay.
rules.experiment: Keep geometry and resources fixed, toggle one mechanism, use matched starts at bottom/rising/top/descending/occupied states, and report each travel phase separately.

rules.principle: Design a teleporter around arrival behavior and subsequent choices as well as displacement.
rules.mechanism: Stock Quake II clears velocity, turns the player, briefly holds movement and can telefrag an occupied destination; the exit is a contestable commitment.
rules.generator_action: Use the native source disc and trigger, supported destination, actual raised arrival hull, explicit yaw, usable escape space and an arrival-threat audit.
rules.counterexample: Zero spawn-to-spawn sightlines does not prevent a nearby spawn from ambushing the teleporter exit.
rules.experiment: Toggle only the teleporter link, compare empty/occupied/repeated arrivals from matched starts, and rotate only exit facing in a separate experiment.

rules.principle: Change room outlines and peek angles where they alter a useful encounter or route.
rules.mechanism: A chamfer or L shaped recess can interrupt a view, reveal a route gradually or provide a distinct recovery position without repeating another room's footprint.
rules.generator_action: Record the exact convex footprint, preserve fighting width, inspect both directions and compare compiled visibility with the coarse layout model.
rules.counterexample: Extra corner cuts can reduce usable space or merely decorate a rectangular tactical plan; aggregate bounding boxes can also hide actual sightlines.
rules.experiment: Change one square corner into a chamfer with items and routes fixed; compare compiled hulls first, then player movement and combat choices.

rules.principle: Treat a ramp as one continuous supported surface with a lower approach and upper landing.
rules.mechanism: An incline changes movement rhythm and exposure only when the full player hull can enter, traverse and leave it; a sloped rendered face or maximum bounding-box height is insufficient.
rules.generator_action: Use an exact supported height function, uphill hull extent, native slope/step bounds, complete end joins and continuous clearance checks. Export signed slope metadata and compare compiled geometry with the authored contract.
rules.counterexample: A valid gentle plane can have an excessive entry lip or blocked exit; a smoother route can expose a player for longer and need not improve combat.
rules.experiment: Replace only one route with an equal-endpoint stair/ramp variant; hold topology, items, widths, cover, settings and starts fixed. Compare native movement and combat outcomes separately.

evidence.observation: gladdm1, trdm05a and spirit2dm9 have supported centerline ramp poses and continuous sweeps; the method is conservative geometry, not engine movement.
Six-plane axial wedges retain continuous height functions; ordinary end joins, hull-aware origins and costs are tested in four directions for Q1/Q2/Q3. Talus uses two 1:4 ramps.

rules.principle: Measure fighting and turning width with the collision hull throughout approaches and exits.
rules.mechanism: Trim, neighboring solids and playerclip can remove lateral choices from a visually broad incline or landing.
rules.generator_action: Check the center and both lateral routes, full standing height, end support and continuous sweeps. Retain rejected lanes and distinguish conservative rejections from confirmed collisions.
rules.counterexample: One clear centerline does not prove the advertised width; a narrow recovery route may be deliberate when its commitment and exit remain useful.
rules.experiment: Change only landing width or intrusive trim, retaining the incline, items and exposure; compare collision evidence first, then turns and contested passage in engine.

evidence.observation: trdm05a's minus-40 lateral lane overlaps brush297; exact convex/AABB overlap confirms the conservative probe's rejection while the center and opposite lane pass.

rules.principle: State required edge kinds and prove ordinary circulation independently of one-way descents and special movement.
rules.mechanism: A visible downward opening can shorten pursuit while concealing a missing return journey; explicit edge filtering distinguishes optional commitment from required circulation.
rules.generator_action: For a no-drop play contract, require every spawn-to-gameplay-anchor pair through walk, step and ordinary door edges only; exclude jump, drop, lift and teleporter edges. Preserve older experiments' explicitly different policies.
measure: spawn-to-anchor pairs under named edge policy
rules.counterexample: A clear landing and a ramp elsewhere do not establish a return loop. Some intentional modes can require a one-way descent, but must declare and validate that commitment separately.
rules.experiment: Keep ordinary routes fixed and enable/close one drop; record pinned game module, gravity, dmflags, water depth, landing velocity/damage, threats and the complete route back.

evidence.observation: At the continuous-movement study stage, gladdm1 and trdm05a descents lacked verified full ordinary returns. The later drop-return study supplies one complete geometric gladdm1 return; trdm05a and native damage remain unverified.
An independent BFS over the exported Talus graph reaches all 264 spawn-to-gameplay pairs through walk/step/door only; no native player traversal is established.
The later gladdm1 certificate separates continuously supported translations from bounded stair changes and retains every world-brush collision check.

rules.principle: Use and label the same coordinate basis when comparing spawn visibility evidence.
rules.mechanism: Cover can block a ray between entity origins while exposing the standing player's eye, producing incompatible safety summaries from unchanged geometry.
rules.generator_action: For stock Q2 spawn pairs, sample entity origin plus 22 Z and export the actual endpoints and offset. Keep other placement roles and Q1/Q3 conventions explicitly distinct; reject invalid eye positions and retain historical sampling provenance.
rules.counterexample: Zero visible spawn pairs does not rule out attacks from a weapon route, upper ledge or teleporter arrival; eye LOS alone is not a spawn-safety guarantee.
rules.experiment: Hold geometry fixed and retain both origin-ray and eye-ray results as a diagnostic; assess the real threat with pinned engine views and matched spawn recovery trials.

evidence.observation: Q2 spawn visibility now uses plus 22 eye height, exports actual samples and rejects eyes inside solids or outside explicit free space.
Visibility reports label player_spawn_eye_offset_z, zero other-placement offset and entity-origin distance basis; navigation graph export preserves these labels.

rules.principle: Validate a material's collision and surface metadata before using it as architecture.
rules.mechanism: A Quake II WAL carries flags and contents as well as pixels; compiler interpretation can turn an authored solid stair or floor into water while it still renders as an architectural surface.
rules.generator_action: Record WAL identity, flags, contents and value; reject liquid/warp metadata for ordinary architectural roles unless deliberately supported. Recompile and require player-mask collision, stair/ramp support and sealed-world checks after a palette change.
rules.counterexample: A texture name resolving successfully, an attractive render or a passing typed solid graph does not prove solid compiled support; intentional liquid volumes must retain their actual contents contract.
rules.experiment: On identical project-authored geometry compare the rejected water/warp WAL against an approved architectural WAL; require the compiled support gate to reject the former before any gameplay test.

evidence.observation: Talus's first palette used mud1_1 on authored architecture; compiled stair-support checks rejected it. The replacement palette uses mine04_1 and must pass the final compiled gates.
CONTENTS_WATER=32, SURF_WARP=8; MASK_PLAYERSOLID does not classify water as ordinary solid support.

rules.principle: Evaluate the complete return as part of a downward shortcut commitment.
rules.mechanism: A quick descent may lead to additional descent, several climbs and an exposed re-entry; binary reachability hides that burden.
rules.generator_action: Record one supported ordinary return with its height profile, route phases, clear widths and exposed sections. State whether it is merely a demonstrated route or an optimized route.
measure: native return time and failed recoveries
rules.counterexample: A connected loop may be too costly under pressure, while a longer hidden section can still be a useful recovery option. The shortest geometric route is not automatically the best combat route.
rules.experiment: Keep the descent fixed and change only one return screen or connection; compare full matched return journeys and outcomes, not only drop time.

evidence.observation: A demonstrated gladdm1 return covers 3088 plan units, climbs 384 and descends another 112 after the initial 272-unit drop; it is not claimed shortest or runtime tested.
Both Undercut descent candidates have exact-height ordinary return bindings, requiring 12 and 10 walk/step edges in the retained BFS paths. Entire compiled return sweeps remain unverified.

rules.principle: Check the landing information available before a player commits to descent.
rules.mechanism: A ledge can offer a useful escape or contest only if its landing and onward options can be understood; the lip itself can hide a lower target from a position set too far back.
rules.generator_action: Retain a full-footprint supported takeoff, clear candidate descent, supported landing and ordinary return. Sample landing visibility at the actual standing eye and test recognition in the engine.
rules.counterexample: A clear eye ray does not establish a readable render, harmless fall or safe landing. Some deliberate blind drops can work, but their information and risk contract must be explicit.
rules.experiment: Change only a landing screen, with the drop and resources fixed; compare advance information, hesitation, interceptions and successful disengagement from matched starts.

evidence.observation: Two fully supported ledge-edge takeoffs have clear landing-eye rays and four clear literal horizontal/vertical swept translations against 178 world solids. These are geometric candidates, not ballistic trajectories.

rules.principle: Verify the compiled intervention rather than assuming unchanged recipe inputs imply a controlled comparison.
rules.mechanism: Replacing a sloped brush with steps can trigger material or compiler changes even when dimensions, light entities and the typed material role are preserved.
rules.generator_action: Compare semantic world brushes and entity properties between conditions, normalize only stable identity fields, and explicitly validate changed face materials. Keep source/compiler/asset hashes and both final artifacts.
measure: unchanged nonintervention brush geometry and material counts
rules.counterexample: A recompiled lightmap can differ with changed geometry without a second authored intervention; it must be recorded, not falsely claimed pixel-identical. Changed texture assignment is an avoidable authored-material confound.
rules.experiment: Replace only Talus Bench ascent with equal-footprint, equal-endpoint stairs; preserve all other geometry/items/lights and match actual architectural face materials before running paired native journeys.

evidence.observation: Talus Bench retains 173 complete source/compiled brush signatures and all 81 nonworld entities. Exactly one ramp becomes eight material-matched treads. Both BSPs pass dedicated initialization; paired native movement remains untested.

rules.principle: Place useful routes beside, around and above one another before shrinking movement clearance.
rules.mechanism: Shared room boundaries and short offset connections can reduce empty peripheral travel while preserving different approach angles.
rules.generator_action: Track gross envelope coverage, actual ordinary routes, route detours and lower/upper use separately. Preserve deliberate courts and sightline separators.
rules.counterexample: A full bounding rectangle can hide solid cores, inaccessible areas or excessive central pressure. Surface packing and movement quality are different quantities.
rules.experiment: Close or relocate one exterior detour with its endpoints, resources and local widths held fixed; measure travel and encounters rather than rewarding coverage alone.

evidence.observation: Reference-specific geometry and native Q2 transfer constraints are retained separately from the design hypothesis.
Fold gross room/passage envelope coverage 94.8% versus Undercut 61.2%, in a 20.2% smaller envelope; internal solids are not subtracted and these values are not playable-density scores.

rules.principle: Give raised interior walkways a purpose above and a usable space below.
rules.mechanism: A partial gallery can provide an alternative approach while its underside shapes a separate lower route or encounter.
rules.generator_action: Export both route stations and their actual heights. Check supported hull sweeps above and below, landing turns, sightline interruptions and exits.
measure: upper and lower continuous hull clearance
rules.counterexample: Projected overlap is not a connection. A walkway can waste the floor below, create an uncontested rail perch or hide a cramped recovery trap.
rules.experiment: Change one walkway screen or width with the same endpoints and items; compare movement, pursuit and lower-player responses.

evidence.observation: Reference-specific geometry and native Q2 transfer constraints are retained separately from the design hypothesis.
Same-XY atrium segments at feet 0/128 both have full-footprint continuous support and clear compiled standing-hull sweeps.

rules.principle: Design a horseshoe as connected arms around a meaningful core with distinct onward choices.
rules.mechanism: The central obstruction separates approach information while the crossbar connects the arms; additional mouths can prevent a forced U-turn.
rules.generator_action: Retain the actual U-shaped free footprint, identify both arm entrances and the crossbar, and audit the complete ordinary path around the core.
rules.counterexample: A U-shaped outline can still be two dead ends or a single long corridor. A filled central core is structure, not automatically wasted exterior void.
rules.experiment: Open or close one secondary arm exit while holding the core and items fixed; observe retreat failures and control of both mouths.

evidence.observation: Reference-specific geometry and native Q2 transfer constraints are retained separately from the design hypothesis.
Three joined flat segments trace the real lower U around its service core with continuous supported hull clearance; native encounter outcomes remain unknown.

rules.principle: Declare whether each crate or barrier is cover, a climbable platform or a route separator.
rules.mechanism: A prop changes peeks, strafe room and access to height; its visual identity should match its collision and landing behavior.
rules.generator_action: For climbable props retain the approach, bounded ascent, supported top and departure. Show local prop heights without inventing a whole additional floor.
rules.counterexample: A crate that looks climbable but has no reliable landing misleads players; scattering crates to raise cover counts can obstruct the entire room.
rules.experiment: Move one crate or change only its height; compare approach choices and congestion before changing the resource it protects.

evidence.observation: Reference-specific geometry and native Q2 transfer constraints are retained separately from the design hypothesis.
The explicit 64-unit crate has a four-step ordinary ascent and a checked flat top segment; it is displayed as a local prop landing, not another whole floor.

rules.principle: Treat liquid as a movement and information commitment with explicit exits.
rules.mechanism: Depth and native contents change waterlevel, friction, swimming, sound and potentially damage; visual shallowness does not imply dry movement.
rules.generator_action: Record liquid bounds, depth, native contents/surface flags, bottom support, entry/exit profiles and air. Keep required dry circulation independent until swim navigation is implemented.
rules.counterexample: A short wet route may be slower and more predictable than a dry detour; a harmless-looking surface can conceal a movement or exit trap.
rules.experiment: Compare the same solid basin wet and dry under pinned physics, then change only one exit. Measure the complete journey and failed attempts.

evidence.observation: Reference-specific geometry and native Q2 transfer constraints are retained separately from the design hypothesis.

The exact 24-deep WATER box preserves explicit surface metadata; two stationary standing samples are submerged. All 264 required dry ordinary paths and an inner wet flat segment are checked, while complete wet/native motion remains untested.

Later Fold and Lockyard controlled trials now demonstrate bounded full wet journeys and retain two failed level-view inputs. This supplements the historical static Fold record; game-module effects remain untested.

rules.principle: Evaluate an open court from useful player positions, including beneath its bridges.
rules.mechanism: A partial upper route can shelter lower crossings while other lanes remain open to sky; a sky roof alone does not describe that contrast.
rules.generator_action: Bind a sealed sky ceiling to its actual room and record clear player viewpoints, overhead obstructions and useful upper/lower routes independently.
measure: first overhead hit and surface role
rules.counterexample: Counting sky faces can label a bridge-covered lane as open; copying a large FFA courtyard into duel can create empty travel.
rules.experiment: Hold the court and items fixed and change one partial gallery or screen; compare lower exposure, upper access and encounter use.

evidence.observation: Manhunt has six sampled upper circuit eyes reaching sky and two roof-covered endpoints; gladdm1 central bridge and lateral sky viewpoints differ.
Three selected court sky rays and same-XY upper/lower routes are checked on a sealed BSP; engine sunlight/render recognition remains unmeasured.

rules.principle: Treat surfacing and the turn onto dry ground as separate parts of a water exit.
rules.mechanism: A valid bottom and reachable water surface do not guarantee enough headroom, a dry lip or room to turn away from the basin.
rules.generator_action: Check full hull emergence columns, bottom-to-exit support profiles and the dry turn; retain failed straight-up or straight-ahead candidates.
measure: continuous exit support and swept hull
dry lip rise and turning clearance
rules.counterexample: The gladdm1 basin starts beneath a roof below the water surface; its ramp reaches a shallow shelf where a sideways turn is needed.
rules.experiment: Keep the basin fixed and alter only one exit or overhead obstruction; compare successful emergence, failed exits and recovery under the same inputs.

evidence.observation: A 896-unit gladdm1 geometric route includes the ramp, shallow shelf and dry lip; a blocked starting emergence and two clear later columns are retained.
Two clear geometric emergence columns flank a blocked surfacing attempt under the roof; successful scripted dives complete the full dry exit in native Q2 3.19 CM/Pmove.

rules.principle: Audit route dependence on individual passages at the actual traversable-surface level.
rules.mechanism: An abstract room can contain disconnected dry stations; merging them can conceal a forced return even when every destination is reachable.
rules.generator_action: Remove one passage node set from the directed ordinary navigation graph; retain which spawn-to-anchor pairs are lost and whether the dependent space is a deliberate optional recess.
measure: lost pairs for each passage closure
rules.counterexample: An optional health recess may intentionally have one mouth. Zero dependencies everywhere is not a universal map-quality target.
rules.experiment: Hold the final graph and items fixed, enable/disable one added return, then close the previously dominant passage. Follow with a physical compiled intervention before gameplay claims.

evidence.observation: On final Lockyard, closing Boiler-Winding loses zero required pairs with the added Court-west-station return; excluding that return as well loses 57. The east health recess intentionally loses eight pairs on its own passage closure.

rules.principle: A submerged shortcut needs an understandable dive commitment and a demonstrated recovery.
rules.mechanism: Water movement can hold a level-view swimmer above a low opening even when the standing hull fits beneath it; the input needed to dive is part of the route.
rules.generator_action: Retain the level-input failure and explicit successful dive sequence, full standing-hull clearance, waterlevel progression and dry arrival. Test discoverability before automatic use.
measure: first-time player recognition and exit threats
rules.counterexample: A scripted dive succeeding does not prove that a first-time player understands the route, survives oxygen/damage or escapes an opponent.
rules.experiment: Keep the culvert fixed and compare level, constant dive and phased dive inputs; later change only the visual entry cue and test first-time players.

evidence.observation: Level-view forward 200/400 stall before the low roof. Constant and phased 30-degree dive profiles complete the standing-hull crossing and dry exit with waterlevel 0-1-2-3-2-1-0, without jump/upmove.

rules.principle: Measure liquid travel with matched commands and the same solid geometry before assigning a shortcut value.
rules.mechanism: Water friction, vertical input, view pitch and exit steps can change both speed and completion; a single geometric distance or speed ratio misses those effects.
rules.generator_action: Pin source, BSP, physics, start state, usercmd sequence and arrival predicate; retain drained controls, full frames, failures and first-goal timing separately from command-budget diagnostics.
measure: first valid goal at declared time resolution
rules.counterexample: Removing water from the same tunnel does not measure the real dry detour. A constant dive profile is not a fastest-route proof or multiplayer result.
rules.experiment: Remove only the water volume, verify unchanged source and compiled solids/entities, and compare matched complete journeys. Then separately measure the actual alternative route.

evidence.observation: Fold level-view forward 400 takes 1680 ms wet versus 1424 drained; forward 200 takes 2560 versus 2128. Results use 16 ms commands and exclude 128 ms verified settling.

Lockyard constant 30-degree dive takes 6400/10048 ms wet at forward 400/200 versus 3920/5904 drained under matching commands. Flat wet attempts fail; oxygen, damage, entities and opponents are outside the harness.

rules.principle: Distinguish reaching an exit plane from regaining the intended movement state at that exit.
rules.mechanism: A player can cross a destination while still falling, overshoot its cover or lack the same grounded movement options as another route.
rules.generator_action: Specify destination lane, floor, stance, water state, ground contact and bounded overshoot. Retain planar crossing and stable arrival as separate observations.
measure: state and velocity at both events
rules.counterexample: A deliberately airborne jump route may want an airborne goal; requiring grounded arrival universally would erase that intended mechanic.
rules.experiment: Compare equal-endpoint ascent profiles with identical starts and inputs; then alter only landing space and test movement recovery without conflating it with horizontal speed.

evidence.observation: Talus forward400 descent crosses the lower station at1968ms in both geometries; stairs remain airborne and reach a grounded goal96ms later. At forward200 the48ms difference includes16ms crossing and32ms subsequent recovery.

Eight predeclared profiles on unchanged Ravel produce5 bounded pauses and3 retained failures. Release needs36.125/23.5 further westward units after landing;9 frame-end samples span128ms. A successful pause does not establish onward doorway traversal or safe falling.

rules.principle: Use graph transition penalties as planning policy until native journey evidence calibrates them.
rules.mechanism: Adding graph nodes and step edges can increase an estimated cost without increasing a player journey under the same commands.
rules.generator_action: Label proxy costs and retain matched native timing before favoring ramps or minimizing stair counts. Keep route purpose, slope, landings and visibility as distinct design variables.
measure: graph cost basis and transition counts
rules.counterexample: A tie on one straight uphill fixture does not make every step penalty wrong; narrow treads, turns, collisions and different movement inputs can change outcomes.
rules.experiment: Replace one ramp by equal-footprint stairs, verify all other source and compiled geometry/materials/entities, then compare native lanes and directions with the same inputs.

evidence.observation: The existing Talus graph adds seven step penalties; all three native uphill lanes tie at1984ms for forward400 and2976ms for forward200 across ramp/stairs.

rules.principle: Read movement position, velocity and contact state together when evaluating traversal geometry.
rules.mechanism: Native stepping can change feet height while preserving a zero stored vertical velocity; continuous support geometry also need not keep a descending player grounded every frame.
rules.generator_action: Retain command-end feet displacement, native velocity and ground contact. Do not infer camera motion, aim disturbance or continuous ground contact from one series or a geometric surface label.
rules.counterexample: A larger discrete position update can be smoothed by a client; more sampled airborne frames do not by themselves prove worse control or a dangerous landing.
rules.experiment: Hold input and complete route endpoints fixed; compare support profiles using native frames, then separately measure camera/aim behavior in a full client test.

evidence.observation: Talus stair ascent makes eight16-unit feet updates with zero stored Zvelocity; ramp ascent spreads the rise across more updates. Both descents contain ungrounded samples. No client rendering or aim trial was performed.

Continuation can stop changing XY against geometry while stored horizontal velocity remains nonzero. Recovery requires position bounds, contact, velocity and a sampled dwell together; no one field is a substitute for the full predicate.

rules.principle: Preserve the space needed to turn around a room core when compacting an interleaved route.
rules.mechanism: Close adjacent corridors can still collide with an inside corner or lose floor support while turning; the continuous player hull determines the usable elbow.
rules.generator_action: Audit full-footprint support and continuous hull sweeps on every side of the turn, including its shared corner. Separate upper/lower routes and verify their actual inter-floor return independently.
